subject: Post-demo: SLO confirmation & customer-led k6 runbook

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — SLO targets & customer-led load test

Hi Sandra / TechSolve ops team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great alignment. Quick recap of the target SLOs we discussed and the ask to move to a customer-led load run: 

- SLO targets (Redwood & TechSolve agreed):
  - Non-streaming text-gen: p95 end-to-end latency <= 200 ms
  - Embeddings/short requests: p95 <= 120 ms
  - Streaming sessions: sustain 80 concurrent streams with per-chunk p95 <= 250 ms
  - Error rate target: < 1% client-visible errors

Next steps we proposed on the call:
1) TechSolve confirms a 3-hour test window (we suggested nights UTC).
2) Redwood provides a k6 baseline and a variant script for your traffic profile.
3) TechSolve provides allowlist IPs / test network details and whether you want Redwood-run or TechSolve-run tests.
4) Define abort criteria and post-run artifacts (logs, traces, full k6/Locust output).

I've attached a k6 baseline template that Rishi will iterate on with load specifics. If you prefer Locust for streaming sessions we can provide a small Locust + websocket example, but k6 + xk6 extensions will work for most of the planned scenarios.

Please confirm the proposed window (we suggested Apr 26 02:00-05:00 UTC on the call) and whether you want Redwood to execute the run or hand over the script and credentials to your ops team.

Thanks —
Naomi

Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the targets we care most about are:

- p95 <= 200ms for text-gen (non-streaming)
- sustained throughput: ~300 requests/sec for batch endpoints during peak window
- streaming concurrency: 80 concurrent sessions (each session sends ~1 token/sec on average)

We can host the test ourselves (TechSolve ops) but would prefer Redwood to run the first execution so we can observe runner behavior and validate metrics collection. After the first run we'll take ownership of repeat runs.

Proposed window: Apr 26 02:00-05:00 UTC — this works for our on-call rotation.

Attached is our internal load plan and list of NATed egress IPs that need to be allowlisted (short CSV). Please confirm Redwood runner IP ranges and provide a test account / API key or instructions for using our dedicated test tenant.

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — SLO targets & customer-led load test

Thanks Sandra — looping in technical details and runbook. Long message but trying to make this operationally actionable.

Run ownership: Redwood will execute the first run (we'll provide the runner hosts and manage ramping). After the first run we'll hand over the k6 script + credentials to your ops team.

Test artifacts we'll provide post-run: k6 summary, Grafana dashboards (token-level charts), request-level traces (sampled), raw k6 output, and a short postmortem if we hit abort criteria.

Allowlist / network: please add the following Redwood egress addresses to your allowlist for the test window:
- 52.23.45.112
- 52.23.45.113
- 3.130.75.20
(we'll confirm exact addresses 48 hours before the run; these are the runner NAT addresses for the region we'll use)

Test account / credentials (temporary):
- Endpoint: https://api.redwood-inference.staging/ts-4827/v1/generate
- API key: redwood-test-TS4827-XXXX (we'll rotate this after the run)
- Username: ts_loadtest_runner@redwood.ai

k6 guidance and mapping to your targets:
- To hit ~300 req/s for the batch endpoint we recommend an arrival-rate scenario in k6 (constant-arrival-rate) with ~320 iterations/sec to allow headroom, with 300s steady-state after a 5-minute ramp. That maps roughly to 150-200 VUs depending on request-timeouts and think time.
- For streaming sessions we recommend using Locust or a k6 extension (xk6-websockets). Plan for 80 concurrent long-lived WebSocket/HTTP2 streams — each simulated client will keep a connection open and send a token-generation heartbeat at ~1 token/sec.
- Warm-up: 10 minutes at 20% of target; ramp to 100% over 10 minutes; steady for 60–120 minutes depending on how long you want sustained load.

Abort criteria (we'll stop the run and investigate):
- Client-visible error rate > 2% for > 2 consecutive minutes
- p95 latency > 350 ms for non-streaming endpoint for > 5 minutes
- Any sustained backend OOM or repeated 5xx spikes indicated in logs

Pre-test priming steps:
- We will exercise a priming pass (low concurrency) for 20 minutes to warm model KV caches — this reduces cold p95s.
- If you use prefix caching based on request signatures, please share the canonical prompt templates so we can include them in warm-up.

Attachments I'll drop into the Drive folder and also attach here: customer_k6_script_v3.js (k6 with arrival-rate scenario and example header handling), ip_allowlist.csv (from TechSolve), and a short runbook checklist.

Let me know if you want different abort thresholds or to run an A/B variant (quantized model variant vs baseline) during the same window — that's feasible but we should keep the first run simple.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SWE, Inference Reliability
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
